assumptions: The NL states that there are twelve finite states but does not provide their exact state names; this model names twelve condition classes from the described dispatch branches.

The exact low-SoC suitability threshold is not specified. The model uses SoC < 0.2 for low-SoC and SoC >= 0.2 for suitable battery discharge, while preserving the explicitly stated 0.95 full-charge threshold.
The NL mentions engine capacity bound eng3_Pmax but not a complete capacity list. The model treats eng3_Pmax as the second diesel/thermal capacity used with DG2 in the last-priority thermal cases.

The model is a condition-classification abstraction: forced guarded transitions reselect the active dispatch state from current PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity values rather than modeling timed mode memory.
Load cut-in/cut-out behavior is under-specified. The model keeps loads cut in during feasible dispatch and asserts load cut-out only in the extreme illegal overload abstraction.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows the priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, LNG is used before diesel units.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
DG1/DG2 are used only as the last priority after RES, batteries, and LNG.

decisions.rationale: Pbat_dismax is used as an external battery discharge capacity/input bound in the dispatch classifier. The NL requires reading time-varying ship/load/resource/capacity inputs and does not provide an internal update law for battery discharge capacity. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics or a forbidden self-assignment.

The guard from ZeroLoadCharge to RESBatteryDischarge intentionally classifies current external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_dismax. These are read inputs, not internal FSM state variables. No NL-grounded write semantics are available.

The guard from ZeroLoadCharge to LNGCoversDemand is an external-input dispatch condition over load, renewable power, SoC, battery capability, and LNG capacity. Writing those variables inside the FSM would be ungrounded.
The guard from ZeroLoadSpare to RESBatteryDischarge correctly depends on external operating-condition inputs. The repair hints explicitly forbid meaningless self-assignments or invented dynamics.
The guard from ZeroLoadSpare to LNGCoversDemand is part of the NL-grounded condition-classification abstraction. Its variables are external inputs/capacity bounds, so no safe DSL edit is available.

The guard from RESCoversCharge to RESBatteryDischarge intentionally reselects a dispatch state when external load/resource/SoC values change. Adding internal writes would misrepresent the EMS as generating those inputs.
The guard from RESCoversCharge to LNGCoversDemand uses external demand/resource/capacity inputs. The NL gives no update rule for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_dismax, or Pgmax.

The guard from RESCoversSpare to RESBatteryDischarge is a valid external-input classification condition. No grounded edit can make these variables internally written without changing the model meaning.

repair_rationale: All selected diagnostics are design warnings about read-only guard variables in an EMS condition-classification abstraction.
The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; these are external environment/plant inputs rather than internal state variables.
Pbat_dismax is likewise a battery discharge capability bound used to decide whether the battery can cover the remaining deficit. The NL provides no formula or event by which the FSM should update it.
Adding writes would either be meaningless self-assignment or invented plant dynamics, both forbidden by the repair instructions.
Removing Pbat_dismax or simplifying the guards would change the dispatch priority/capacity classification and risk violating preserved NL-grounded states and transitions.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

decisions.rationale: Pbat_dismax is used as an external battery discharge capacity/input bound in the dispatch classifier. The NL requires reading time-varying ship/load/resource/capacity inputs and does not provide an internal update law for battery discharge capacity. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics or a forbidden self-assignment.

The guard from ZeroLoadCharge to RESBatteryDischarge intentionally classifies current external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_dismax. These are read inputs, not internal FSM state variables. No NL-grounded write semantics are available.

The guard from ZeroLoadCharge to LNGCoversDemand is an external-input dispatch condition over load, renewable power, SoC, battery capability, and LNG capacity. Writing those variables inside the FSM would be ungrounded.
The guard from ZeroLoadSpare to RESBatteryDischarge correctly depends on external operating-condition inputs. The repair hints explicitly forbid meaningless self-assignments or invented dynamics.
The guard from ZeroLoadSpare to LNGCoversDemand is part of the NL-grounded condition-classification abstraction. Its variables are external inputs/capacity bounds, so no safe DSL edit is available.

The guard from RESCoversCharge to RESBatteryDischarge intentionally reselects a dispatch state when external load/resource/SoC values change. Adding internal writes would misrepresent the EMS as generating those inputs.
The guard from RESCoversCharge to LNGCoversDemand uses external demand/resource/capacity inputs. The NL gives no update rule for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_dismax, or Pgmax.

The guard from RESCoversSpare to RESBatteryDischarge is a valid external-input classification condition. No grounded edit can make these variables internally written without changing the model meaning.
The guard from RESCoversSpare to LNGCoversDemand depends on externally supplied load, renewable, SoC, and capacity values. The safest repair is to preserve the guard and request waiver/override.
The self-reselection guard for RESBatteryDischarge is expected in a condition-classification FSM driven by external operating inputs. It should not be silenced by dummy writes.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit produced. All requests rejected/waived because the warnings correspond to intentional external-input guard variables, and no safe NL-grounded internal write exists.

repair_rationale: All selected diagnostics are design warnings about read-only guard variables in an EMS condition-classification abstraction.
The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; these are external environment/plant inputs rather than internal state variables.
Pbat_dismax is likewise a battery discharge capability bound used to decide whether the battery can cover the remaining deficit. The NL provides no formula or event by which the FSM should update it.
Adding writes would either be meaningless self-assignment or invented plant dynamics, both forbidden by the repair instructions.
Removing Pbat_dismax or simplifying the guards would change the dispatch priority/capacity classification and risk violating preserved NL-grounded states and transitions.

decisions.rationale: Pbat_dismax is used as an external battery discharge capacity/input bound in the dispatch classifier. The NL requires reading time-varying ship/load/resource/capacity inputs and does not provide an internal update law for battery discharge capacity. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics or a forbidden self-assignment.

The guard from ZeroLoadCharge to RESBatteryDischarge intentionally classifies current external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_dismax. These are read inputs, not internal FSM state variables. No NL-grounded write semantics are available.

The guard from ZeroLoadCharge to LNGCoversDemand is an external-input dispatch condition over load, renewable power, SoC, battery capability, and LNG capacity. Writing those variables inside the FSM would be ungrounded.
The guard from ZeroLoadSpare to RESBatteryDischarge correctly depends on external operating-condition inputs. The repair hints explicitly forbid meaningless self-assignments or invented dynamics.
The guard from ZeroLoadSpare to LNGCoversDemand is part of the NL-grounded condition-classification abstraction. Its variables are external inputs/capacity bounds, so no safe DSL edit is available.

The guard from RESCoversCharge to RESBatteryDischarge intentionally reselects a dispatch state when external load/resource/SoC values change. Adding internal writes would misrepresent the EMS as generating those inputs.
The guard from RESCoversCharge to LNGCoversDemand uses external demand/resource/capacity inputs. The NL gives no update rule for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_dismax, or Pgmax.

The guard from RESCoversSpare to RESBatteryDischarge is a valid external-input classification condition. No grounded edit can make these variables internally written without changing the model meaning.
The guard from RESCoversSpare to LNGCoversDemand depends on externally supplied load, renewable, SoC, and capacity values. The safest repair is to preserve the guard and request waiver/override.
The self-reselection guard for RESBatteryDischarge is expected in a condition-classification FSM driven by external operating inputs. It should not be silenced by dummy writes.
The guard from RESBatteryDischarge to LNGCoversDemand is controlled by external inputs and capacity bounds. This is NL-faithful for an EMS that reads changing operating conditions.
The guard from LNGCoversDemand to RESBatteryDischarge is an external-input dispatch transition. There is no NL-grounded internal state update that would safely address the warning.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit produced. All requests rejected/waived because the warnings correspond to intentional external-input guard variables, and no safe NL-grounded internal write exists.

repair_rationale: All selected diagnostics are design warnings about read-only guard variables in an EMS condition-classification abstraction.
The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; these are external environment/plant inputs rather than internal state variables.
Pbat_dismax is likewise a battery discharge capability bound used to decide whether the battery can cover the remaining deficit. The NL provides no formula or event by which the FSM should update it.
Adding writes would either be meaningless self-assignment or invented plant dynamics, both forbidden by the repair instructions.
Removing Pbat_dismax or simplifying the guards would change the dispatch priority/capacity classification and risk violating preserved NL-grounded states and transitions.

scenario_results.description: default-init: with PL=0 and SoC below 0.95, first cycle dispatches to zero-load battery charging from RES production.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_charge

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at the SoC=0.95 boundary with PL=0, RES production should become spare power rather than battery charge.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_soc_full_spare_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when RES covers positive PL and SoC is just below 0.95, serve load from RES and charge the surplus.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when RES covers positive PL and SoC is at least 0.95, surplus RES should be reported as spare power.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at the SoC=0.2 suitability boundary, RES shortfall within battery discharge capacity should be supplied by battery.
scenario_results.name: battery_discharge_at_soc_suitable_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC but residual demand above battery discharge capacity and within LNG capacity, LNG should cut in before diesel units.
scenario_results.name: lng_covers_after_battery_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC and residual demand coverable by LNG plus Pgmax/5 margin, LNG should charge battery using that margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and residual demand exceeding LNG but within LNG+DG1 capacity, DG1 should cut in as the next thermal priority.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_covers_after_lng_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC in the LNG+DG1 region, add the Pd1max/10 charging margin while keeping DG2 out.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and residual demand exceeding LNG+DG1 but within all thermal capacity, DG2 should cut in last.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_covers_after_dg1_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC in the all-thermal covered region, add the Pd1max/10 charging margin while all thermal units are active.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when demand exceeds RES plus all thermal resources, activate all thermal units, cover the lack by battery discharge, and cut out loads in the illegal overload abstraction.
scenario_results.name: extreme_overload_all_thermal_battery_lack

evidence: For `SoC < 0.2`, residual demand within LNG capacity but above `0.8 * Pgmax` fails `LNGLowSoCChargeMargin` and also fails DG/extreme guards.
Similar holes occur in later low-SoC diesel-generator margin regions when margin addition exceeds available capacity while demand itself is still within available thermal capacity.
The NL requires dynamic dispatch over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC; it does not permit unclassified feasible regions.

evidence: NL: "It controls power dispatch between generating units and load demand during changing time periods and operating conditions, dynamically switching states to maintain power balance as resources and demands vary."
DSL low-SoC LNG branch guard: `SoC < 0.2 && PL - Ppv - Pw + Pgmax / 5 <= Pgmax`.

Counterexample region: `SoC < 0.2`, `0 < PL - Ppv - Pw <= Pgmax`, but `PL - Ppv - Pw + Pgmax / 5 > Pgmax`; no LNG low-SoC state matches, no DG state matches because residual is not `> Pgmax`, and extreme state does not match because residual is not `> Pgmax + Pd1max + eng3_Pmax`.
Analogous holes exist for low-SoC DG1/DG2 margin regions when residual demand is within available thermal capacity but adding the required charging margin exceeds the relevant capacity bound.
findings.summary: Low-SoC dispatch is not total over feasible demand/capacity regions, so the EMS can fail to select any state even though the NL requires dynamic state switching to maintain power balance as resources and demands vary.

evidence: sim_summary: `n_scenarios: 15`, `n_scenarios_passed: 15`.
Provided passing low-SoC LNG scenario uses `PL=100`, `Ppv=20`, `Pw=10`, `Pgmax=100`, so residual is 70 and residual + Pgmax/5 is 90, safely within capacity.
No shown scenario tests low-SoC residual in `(0.8 * Pgmax, Pgmax]`, where the LNG demand is feasible but the margin guard rejects the branch.
Transition sample shows only margin forms for low SoC, not fallback demand-covering states without charge margin.
findings.summary: The simulation oracle passes sampled cases but misses boundary/near-capacity low-SoC cases where all forced transition guards can be false.

evidence: NL: "manages a ship energy system with PVs, WECs, DGs, LNG, batteries, and time-varying ship loads, issuing cut-in and cut-out commands for generating units and loads."
DSL variables include `cmd_lng_cut_in/out`, `cmd_dg1_cut_in/out`, `cmd_dg2_cut_in/out`, and `cmd_load_cut_in/out`.
DSL has no PV/WEC cut-in/cut-out commands and no battery cut-in/cut-out commands; PV/WEC appear only as input power contributions `Ppv` and `Pw`.
findings.summary: Major physical components and outputs are represented, but cut-in/cut-out command coverage is limited to LNG, DG1, DG2, and load commands; PV/WEC or battery command semantics are not modeled.

evidence: NL: "The overload completion state is illegal ... the state shall never occur in practice."
DSL guard makes `ExtremeAllThermalBattery` reachable when `PL - Ppv - Pw > Pgmax + Pd1max + eng3_Pmax`.
DSL action sets all thermal units active and `cmd_load_cut_out = 1`, which gives some fail-safe semantics.
DSL action sets `Pbat_dis = PL - Ppv - Pw - Pgmax - Pd1max - eng3_Pmax` without guard against `Pbat_dismax` or low SoC, and no diagnostic flag marks the illegal condition.
findings.summary: The illegal overload state is modeled as a reachable fail-safe-like branch with load cut-out, which is admissible in principle, but it lacks an explicit diagnostic/violation output and can command battery discharge without checking battery discharge capability.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics: `n_transitions_forced: 144`, `n_events: 0`, `n_transitions_normal: 1`.
Grounding assumption: "condition-classification abstraction ... rather than modeling timed mode memory."
DSL states assign outputs on entry, but there are no events or internal time-period variables.
findings.summary: The FSM is mostly a combinational classifier implemented by forced `! *` transitions rather than persistent operating modes; this is an acceptable abstraction for condition classification but should not be overinterpreted as time-mode behavior.

evidence: NL references "changing time periods and operating conditions" and "time-varying ship loads".
DSL has no event declarations and no time/period variable; state selection depends only on current `PL`, `Ppv`, `Pw`, `SoC`, and capacity values.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics: `n_events: 0`.
findings.summary: Time-varying ship loads and operating periods are represented only by instantaneous external inputs; no time-period, forecast, hysteresis, ramping, or persistence behavior is modeled.

decisions.rationale: Pbat_dismax is an externally read battery discharge capacity bound used to classify dispatch. The NL says the FSM reads load, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide an internal update law for Pbat_dismax. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden.

The ZeroLoadCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally depends on current external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_dismax. These variables represent operating conditions and capability bounds, not internal FSM state to be updated by actions.

The ZeroLoadCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-grounded dispatch condition over external demand, renewable power, battery capability, SoC, and LNG capacity. No safe NL-grounded write exists for those inputs.

The ZeroLoadSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard correctly reclassifies the EMS state when externally supplied demand/resource/SoC/capacity values change. Editing it to silence the warning would weaken the dispatch priority model.

The ZeroLoadSpare to LNGCoversDemand guard is part of the condition-classification abstraction over external operating inputs. The NL provides no internal dynamics for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_dismax, or Pgmax.

The RESCoversCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally reacts to changing external load, renewable power, SoC, and battery discharge capability. Adding writes would misrepresent the EMS as producing those inputs.

The RESCoversCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-faithful capacity/priority dispatch condition. A repair would require ungrounded updates to external inputs or removal of required classification logic.

The RESCoversSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard depends on external operating-condition variables. The warning is conservative for this combinational classifier abstraction, and no safe DSL edit is supported by the NL.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit produced. All 12 requests are rejected with waiver rationale because the diagnostics concern intentional external-input guard variables in an NL-grounded EMS dispatch classifier.

repair_rationale: All current requests repeat the same warning class already rejected and waived in the FixLog: read-only external input/capacity variables drive condition-classification guards.

The NL explicitly says the EMS reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds such as eng3_Pmax; Pbat_dismax is likewise a battery discharge capability bound needed to decide whether the battery can cover the remaining deficit.

The required preserve list includes all twelve dispatch states and the classification transition structure. Removing Pbat_dismax from guards, replacing guards with constants, or adding dummy writes would either violate dispatch semantics or create ungrounded plant dynamics.

decisions.rationale: Pbat_dismax is an externally read battery discharge capacity bound used to classify dispatch. The NL says the FSM reads load, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide an internal update law for Pbat_dismax. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden.

The ZeroLoadCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally depends on current external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_dismax. These variables represent operating conditions and capability bounds, not internal FSM state to be updated by actions.

The ZeroLoadCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-grounded dispatch condition over external demand, renewable power, battery capability, SoC, and LNG capacity. No safe NL-grounded write exists for those inputs.

The ZeroLoadSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard correctly reclassifies the EMS state when externally supplied demand/resource/SoC/capacity values change. Editing it to silence the warning would weaken the dispatch priority model.

The ZeroLoadSpare to LNGCoversDemand guard is part of the condition-classification abstraction over external operating inputs. The NL provides no internal dynamics for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_dismax, or Pgmax.

The RESCoversCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally reacts to changing external load, renewable power, SoC, and battery discharge capability. Adding writes would misrepresent the EMS as producing those inputs.

The RESCoversCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-faithful capacity/priority dispatch condition. A repair would require ungrounded updates to external inputs or removal of required classification logic.

The RESCoversSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard depends on external operating-condition variables. The warning is conservative for this combinational classifier abstraction, and no safe DSL edit is supported by the NL.

The RESCoversSpare to LNGCoversDemand guard must preserve external demand/resource/capacity classification. Simplifying or internally writing the guard variables would violate the stated dispatch logic.

The RESBatteryDischarge self-reselection guard is expected in a classifier FSM that continuously reselects states from current external conditions. The prior FixLog already rejected this same repair class, and no new evidence justifies inventing updates.

The RESBatteryDischarge to LNGCoversDemand guard is controlled by external load, renewable, SoC, battery capability, and LNG capacity values. It is required for the priority transition from battery support to LNG coverage.

The LNGCoversDemand to RESBatteryDischarge guard is an external-input dispatch transition. There is no NL-grounded internal state update that would safely address W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE without changing model meaning.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

decisions.rationale: Pbat_dismax is an externally read battery discharge capacity bound used to classify dispatch. The NL says the FSM reads load, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide an internal update law for Pbat_dismax. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden.

The ZeroLoadCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally depends on current external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_dismax. These variables represent operating conditions and capability bounds, not internal FSM state to be updated by actions.

The ZeroLoadCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-grounded dispatch condition over external demand, renewable power, battery capability, SoC, and LNG capacity. No safe NL-grounded write exists for those inputs.

The ZeroLoadSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard correctly reclassifies the EMS state when externally supplied demand/resource/SoC/capacity values change. Editing it to silence the warning would weaken the dispatch priority model.

The ZeroLoadSpare to LNGCoversDemand guard is part of the condition-classification abstraction over external operating inputs. The NL provides no internal dynamics for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_dismax, or Pgmax.

The RESCoversCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally reacts to changing external load, renewable power, SoC, and battery discharge capability. Adding writes would misrepresent the EMS as producing those inputs.

The RESCoversCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-faithful capacity/priority dispatch condition. A repair would require ungrounded updates to external inputs or removal of required classification logic.

The RESCoversSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard depends on external operating-condition variables. The warning is conservative for this combinational classifier abstraction, and no safe DSL edit is supported by the NL.

The RESCoversSpare to LNGCoversDemand guard must preserve external demand/resource/capacity classification. Simplifying or internally writing the guard variables would violate the stated dispatch logic.

The RESBatteryDischarge self-reselection guard is expected in a classifier FSM that continuously reselects states from current external conditions. The prior FixLog already rejected this same repair class, and no new evidence justifies inventing updates.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit produced. All 12 requests are rejected with waiver rationale because the diagnostics concern intentional external-input guard variables in an NL-grounded EMS dispatch classifier.

repair_rationale: All current requests repeat the same warning class already rejected and waived in the FixLog: read-only external input/capacity variables drive condition-classification guards.

The NL explicitly says the EMS reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds such as eng3_Pmax; Pbat_dismax is likewise a battery discharge capability bound needed to decide whether the battery can cover the remaining deficit.

The required preserve list includes all twelve dispatch states and the classification transition structure. Removing Pbat_dismax from guards, replacing guards with constants, or adding dummy writes would either violate dispatch semantics or create ungrounded plant dynamics.
Because no request can be safely accepted, the SL-9 contract requires leaving candidate_dsl empty rather than emitting an unchanged or unsafe repaired DSL.

decisions.rationale: Pbat_dismax is an externally read battery discharge capacity bound used to classify dispatch. The NL says the FSM reads load, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide an internal update law for Pbat_dismax. Adding a write would invent plant dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden.

The ZeroLoadCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally depends on current external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_dismax. These variables represent operating conditions and capability bounds, not internal FSM state to be updated by actions.

The ZeroLoadCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-grounded dispatch condition over external demand, renewable power, battery capability, SoC, and LNG capacity. No safe NL-grounded write exists for those inputs.

The ZeroLoadSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard correctly reclassifies the EMS state when externally supplied demand/resource/SoC/capacity values change. Editing it to silence the warning would weaken the dispatch priority model.

The ZeroLoadSpare to LNGCoversDemand guard is part of the condition-classification abstraction over external operating inputs. The NL provides no internal dynamics for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_dismax, or Pgmax.

The RESCoversCharge to RESBatteryDischarge guard intentionally reacts to changing external load, renewable power, SoC, and battery discharge capability. Adding writes would misrepresent the EMS as producing those inputs.

The RESCoversCharge to LNGCoversDemand guard is an NL-faithful capacity/priority dispatch condition. A repair would require ungrounded updates to external inputs or removal of required classification logic.

The RESCoversSpare to RESBatteryDischarge guard depends on external operating-condition variables. The warning is conservative for this combinational classifier abstraction, and no safe DSL edit is supported by the NL.

The RESCoversSpare to LNGCoversDemand guard must preserve external demand/resource/capacity classification. Simplifying or internally writing the guard variables would violate the stated dispatch logic.

The RESBatteryDischarge self-reselection guard is expected in a classifier FSM that continuously reselects states from current external conditions. The prior FixLog already rejected this same repair class, and no new evidence justifies inventing updates.

The RESBatteryDischarge to LNGCoversDemand guard is controlled by external load, renewable, SoC, battery capability, and LNG capacity values. It is required for the priority transition from battery support to LNG coverage.

The LNGCoversDemand to RESBatteryDischarge guard is an external-input dispatch transition. There is no NL-grounded internal state update that would safely address W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE without changing model meaning.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit produced. All 12 requests are rejected with waiver rationale because the diagnostics concern intentional external-input guard variables in an NL-grounded EMS dispatch classifier.

repair_rationale: All current requests repeat the same warning class already rejected and waived in the FixLog: read-only external input/capacity variables drive condition-classification guards.

The NL explicitly says the EMS reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds such as eng3_Pmax; Pbat_dismax is likewise a battery discharge capability bound needed to decide whether the battery can cover the remaining deficit.

The required preserve list includes all twelve dispatch states and the classification transition structure. Removing Pbat_dismax from guards, replacing guards with constants, or adding dummy writes would either violate dispatch semantics or create ungrounded plant dynamics.
Because no request can be safely accepted, the SL-9 contract requires leaving candidate_dsl empty rather than emitting an unchanged or unsafe repaired DSL.

scenario_results.description: default-init: with PL=0 and SoC below 0.95, first cycle dispatches to zero-load battery charging from RES production.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_charge

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at the SoC=0.95 boundary with PL=0, RES production should become spare power rather than battery charge.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_soc_full_spare_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when RES covers positive PL and SoC is just below 0.95, serve load from RES and charge the surplus.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when RES covers positive PL and SoC is at least 0.95, surplus RES should be reported as spare power.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at the SoC=0.2 suitability boundary, RES shortfall within battery discharge capacity should be supplied by battery.
scenario_results.name: battery_discharge_at_soc_suitable_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC but residual demand above battery discharge capacity and within LNG capacity, LNG should cut in before diesel units.
scenario_results.name: lng_covers_after_battery_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC and residual demand coverable by LNG plus Pgmax/5 margin, LNG should charge battery using that margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and residual demand exceeding LNG but within LNG+DG1 capacity, DG1 should cut in as the next thermal priority.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_covers_after_lng_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC in the LNG+DG1 region, add the Pd1max/10 charging margin while keeping DG2 out.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and residual demand exceeding LNG+DG1 but within all thermal capacity, DG2 should cut in last.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_covers_after_dg1_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC in the all-thermal covered region, add the Pd1max/10 charging margin while all thermal units are active.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when demand exceeds RES plus all thermal resources, activate all thermal units, cover the lack by battery discharge, and cut out loads in the illegal overload abstraction.
scenario_results.name: extreme_overload_all_thermal_battery_lack

evidence: DSL low-SoC LNG guard requires `PL - Ppv - Pw + Pgmax / 5 <= Pgmax`.
With `SoC < 0.2` and residual demand in `(0.8*Pgmax, Pgmax]`, the low-SoC LNG state is not selected, while `LNGCoversDemand` is excluded by `SoC >= 0.2`.
Analogous gaps occur for low-SoC DG1/DG2 margin states near their capacity limits.
NL requires logical state selection over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC and dispatch that maintains power balance.
blocking_findings.summary: The low-SoC dispatch guards leave feasible demand regions with no matching state, so the FSM can fail to maintain power balance despite the NL requiring state selection and dynamic power-balance dispatch.

evidence: DSL low-SoC LNG guard: `SoC < 0.2 && PL - Ppv - Pw + Pgmax / 5 <= Pgmax`, equivalent to residual demand <= 0.8*Pgmax.
For `SoC < 0.2`, `Ppv+Pw < PL`, and residual demand in `(0.8*Pgmax, Pgmax]`, no LNG low-SoC state matches and the suitable-SoC LNG state is excluded by `SoC >= 0.2`.

Similar low-SoC gaps exist around the DG1 and DG2 capacity boundaries because the margin guards require `residual + Pd1max/10 <= capacity` while the non-margin covered-demand states require `SoC >= 0.2`.

NL: `dynamically switching states to maintain power balance as resources and demands vary` and `The twelve finite states are selected by logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC.`
findings.summary: The low-SoC dispatch guards leave feasible demand regions with no matching state, so the FSM can fail to maintain power balance even though the NL says the twelve states are selected by logical conditions and dispatch dynamically maintains balance.

evidence: sim_summary: `n_scenarios: 15`, `n_scenarios_passed: 15`.
Covered low-SoC examples use values that satisfy the margin guards, e.g. `lng_low_soc_charge_margin` has residual 70 and `Pgmax/5` margin 20 with `Pgmax=100`, so 90 <= 100.
No shown scenario tests low SoC with residual demand between 80 and 100 for `Pgmax=100`, or analogous DG1/DG2 near-capacity low-SoC cases.
findings.summary: Scenario coverage does not exercise the uncovered low-SoC boundary regions where charging margins cannot fit within available thermal capacity.

evidence: NL: `The overload completion state is illegal... the state shall never occur in practice.`
DSL has reachable forced transition: `! * -> ExtremeAllThermalBattery : if [PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw < PL && PL - Ppv - Pw > Pgmax + Pd1max + eng3_Pmax]`.

DSL action in `ExtremeAllThermalBattery` activates all thermal units and sets `cmd_load_cut_in = 0; cmd_load_cut_out = 1;`, providing fail-safe semantics, but no explicit diagnostic or illegal-state output variable is modeled.
findings.summary: The illegal overload branch is reachable and performs a load cut-out fail-safe action, which may be an admitted abstraction, but it does not explicitly mark the violation with a diagnostic/illegal flag beyond the state name and output pattern.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics: `n_transitions_forced: 144`, `n_events: 0`, `n_transitions_normal: 1`.
Grounding assumption: `condition-classification abstraction ... rather than modeling timed mode memory.`
NL mentions `changing time periods and operating conditions`; the DSL has no event or internal time-period variable.
findings.summary: The FSM is primarily a combinational condition classifier using forced all-state transitions rather than persistent operating modes or time-period behavior.

evidence: NL: `controls power dispatch ... during changing time periods and operating conditions, dynamically switching states`.
DSL uses only current values of `PL`, `Ppv`, `Pw`, `SoC`, and capacity bounds in forced guards.
No events, timers, history variables, or mode-memory variables are present.
findings.summary: The model abstracts time-varying ship operation into instantaneous reclassification; acceptable as a dispatch-condition abstraction but weaker than the NL's dynamic operating-period description.

evidence: Grounding assumption: `The exact low-SoC suitability threshold is not specified. The model uses SoC < 0.2 ...`
Grounding assumption: `The NL mentions engine capacity bound eng3_Pmax but not a complete capacity list. The model treats eng3_Pmax as the second diesel/thermal capacity used with DG2.`
Grounding assumption: `Load cut-in/cut-out behavior is under-specified.`
DSL introduces `Pbat_dismax` although the NL names `eng3_Pmax` as an example capacity bound and does not explicitly name a battery discharge maximum.
findings.summary: Several key modeling choices are assumptions not explicit in the NL, increasing risk against a hidden reference.

evidence: sim_summary: all 15 scenarios pass.
The low-SoC margin examples verify only cases where the added margin fits.
No scenario evidence shows that every combination of low SoC, feasible demand, and thermal capacity selects a valid dispatch state.
findings.summary: The passing simulation suite is not a strong oracle for correctness because it verifies nominal branch examples but misses guard-completeness and boundary-partition cases.

accepted_edit_intent: Broaden LNGLowSoCChargeMargin guard to cover all low-SoC residual demand up to Pgmax.
Broaden LNGDG1LowSoCChargeMargin guard to cover all low-SoC residual demand above Pgmax up to Pgmax + Pd1max.
Broaden LNGDG1DG2LowSoCChargeMargin guard to cover all low-SoC residual demand above Pgmax + Pd1max up to total thermal capacity.
Add conditional enter actions so low-SoC charging margins are applied only when remaining capacity headroom permits.
decisions.rationale: The evidence identifies real low-SoC guard coverage gaps. I accepted the request and broadened the three low-SoC thermal dispatch guards so every feasible residual-demand interval up to the relevant thermal capacity selects a state. To avoid over-requesting generation beyond capacity, the explicit charging margins remain in the state actions only when headroom exists; otherwise the same state covers demand without charging.

accepted_edit_intent: Repair low-SoC dispatch guard completeness while preserving all twelve required states and external-input classification semantics.

finding_summaries.summary: The candidate broadly covers the NL-described EMS components: twelve dispatch states, core external inputs, generator/battery/spare outputs, and cut-in/cut-out commands are represented.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary assumption: `The exact low-SoC suitability threshold is not specified. The model uses SoC < 0.2 ...`.

GroundingMap source_summary assumption: `The NL mentions engine capacity bound eng3_Pmax but not a complete capacity list. The model treats eng3_Pmax as the second diesel/thermal capacity used with DG2 ...`.

finding_summaries.summary: Several dispatch thresholds and capacity mappings are modeling assumptions rather than explicit NL requirements, so fidelity is plausible but not reference-strong.

finding_summaries.summary: The FSM is primarily an instantaneous condition classifier implemented with forced all-state transitions, not a persistent time-period mode machine.

evidence: NL: `controls power dispatch ... during changing time periods and operating conditions, dynamically switching states`.
DSL guards use current values of PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pgmax, Pd1max, eng3_Pmax, and Pbat_dismax.
No events, timers, history variables, or explicit time-period variables are present.
finding_summaries.summary: The model abstracts the NL's time-varying operating conditions into reclassification on current inputs only; this is acceptable as a dispatch-condition abstraction but weaker than a dynamic EMS model.

evidence: NL: `The overload completion state is illegal ... the state shall never occur in practice`.
DSL transition: `! * -> ExtremeAllThermalBattery : if [PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw < PL && PL - Ppv - Pw > Pgmax + Pd1max + eng3_Pmax]`.
ExtremeAllThermalBattery.enter sets all thermal cut-in commands to 1 and sets `cmd_load_cut_in = 0; cmd_load_cut_out = 1`.
No explicit diagnostic/illegal flag is modeled beyond the state name and fail-safe output pattern.
finding_summaries.summary: The illegal overload state is reachable, but it has fail-safe semantics by activating all thermal units and cutting out loads; therefore this is advisory rather than blocking under the review guidance.

evidence: sim_summary.ok = true with 15/15 scenarios passing.
Scenario samples cover the main named states, but the summary does not show negative/no-transition tests for alternate capacity orderings or under-specified thresholds.
warning_budget_exhausted includes many `W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE` entries, consistent with a classifier whose guards were not stress-tested as a full numeric partition.
finding_summaries.summary: Simulation coverage is branch-positive but weak as an oracle for numeric guard partition quality and hidden-reference assumptions.

evidence: sim_summary.n_scenarios = 15 and all pass.
Scenario descriptions are positive examples for the modeled state branches, such as `lng_low_soc_charge_margin`, `lng_dg1_low_soc_charge_margin`, and `extreme_overload_all_thermal_battery_lack`.
No sampled scenario demonstrates adversarial guard-boundary or overlap testing beyond selected SoC boundaries.
finding_summaries.summary: Evaluation risk remains because passing simulations largely mirror the modeled branches and do not prove exhaustive dispatch behavior.
